picks.file: Theatri praecipvarvm totivs mvndi vrbivm - liber sextvs 1618 (97691020).jpg
picks.what: View across the Guadalquivir, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 6
picks.why: colored copy; walled city behind the Roman bridge and the Calahorra tower; legend boxes and book margins cut (faint gutter fold in the middle)

picks.what: Panorama, drawing for the account of Cosimo de’ Medici’s journey through Spain (National Library of Portugal)
picks.why: only view for the period; firmly dated general view of the walled city; gray and low contrast

picks.file: Vista de Córdoba - F. J. Parcerisa.png
picks.what: The Roman bridge and the Mosque-Cathedral across the Guadalquivir, lithograph in Recuerdos y bellezas de España
picks.why: river view with the bridge, the Mosque-Cathedral and its bell tower; title and margins cut

picks.what: The Roman bridge, the Calahorra tower and the Mosque-Cathedral, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color; the city’s three landmarks in one frame; only 1024 px wide; 40 years after the Parcerisa

picks.what: The Mosque-Cathedral from the left bank of the Guadalquivir, photograph
picks.why: sharp sunny view of the Mosque-Cathedral and its bell tower above the river walls

gaps: P0: no candidates. P3: nothing (#7 is Córdoba, Argentina; #8 is a history painting). P5: no candidates
notes: P1 alternatives: #3, an uncolored Italian print of the same composition dated 1585–90 by the Biblioteca Nacional de España (apparently the model for the Braun and Hogenberg plate), and the 1567 Wyngaerde panorama (#4, 8:1 strip, too narrow for the card). Baldi is not named on Commons but drew the views for Cosimo de’ Medici’s 1668–69 journey. #10 photochrom: LOC date field says 1890; labeled 1890s per the photochrom rule. Bossuet painting (#14) undated, skipped. Excluded Córdoba, Argentina (#7, #16), Córdoba, Veracruz (#20, #21), reservoir in the province (#19), and Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba hits (#5, #8).
